All21 Reference18 UMI≥50: disease-blind K=3 spatial niche analysis

Rendered 2026-10-11T19:55:38; report ID 261011195538

Approved scope. One common disease-blind K=3 niche atlas across 21 patients, followed by patient-level HC, IPF and SSc-ILD comparisons. K=4 was an accidental exploratory run and is excluded from this report.

1. Goal and analysis design

Construct local spatial neighborhoods from frozen Reference18 RCTD weights, describe each niche by its cell-type mixture, and test disease-associated changes in niche abundance and niche–niche adjacency without treating bins as independent biological replicates.

2. K audit and interpretation boundary

K=3 was retained as the most parsimonious and most repeat-stable candidate. Chip-centering reduced chip association, but held-chip transfer remained below the predeclared validation threshold. K=3 is therefore an exploratory common resolution, not a fully validated universal atlas.

4. Spatial localization across patients

Assignments are displayed separately for all 21 patients. Visual recurrence and spatial coherence are necessary descriptive checks, while patient-level statistics below provide inference.

5. Disease comparison of niche abundance

Each point represents one patient. Disease effects were estimated from corrected-logit niche fractions with chip as a covariate and evaluated using 10,000 within-chip disease-label permutations.

6. Disease comparison of niche–niche adjacency

Within each patient, adjacency enrichment is log2(observed/expected) for bins separated by ≤36 µm. Expected counts preserve patient-specific niche abundance. Disease inference again uses patients as replicates, chip adjustment and within-chip permutations.

7. Conclusions

  • The K=3 heatmap provides an interpretable descriptive summary of three mixed tissue-composition niches.
  • No niche-abundance contrast passed permutation FDR <0.05.
  • No inter-niche adjacency contrast passed permutation FDR <0.05.
  • These null results do not establish biological equivalence; the atlas is exploratory and between-patient heterogeneity is substantial.
  • The next justified layer is patient × niche pseudobulk analysis of raw gene counts and predeclared fibrosis, epithelial injury, vascular-remodeling and immune gene programs.
